findings.title: The unsubscribe route cannot find its template
findings.body: This declares `topicUnsubscribe` as a top-level route, whose template name is `topic-unsubscribe`, but the added template is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which corresponds to a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. No custom template mapping is provided, so navigating to the unsubscribe URL will not render the confirmation page and may fail with a missing-template error.

findings.title: A GET request changes notification preferences
findings.body: The unsubscribe route is a GET endpoint, and this action changes and saves the user's notification level as part of handling that request. Email security scanners, link prefetchers, or a cross-site link opened with the user's session can therefore change that user's topic preferences without an intentional confirmation. Use a non-mutating confirmation page followed by a state-changing request, or another mechanism that prevents accidental and cross-site changes.

findings.title: The action crashes when the user has no topic-user row
findings.body: `find_by` can return `nil` for a user who has not yet acquired a `TopicUser` row for this topic, but the next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`. Opening the unsubscribe URL in that case raises an exception instead of showing the page or changing the preference; handle the missing row or create it through the normal TopicUser API.

findings.title: Saving directly bypasses TopicUser notification-change behavior
findings.body: Calling `save!` directly does not apply the bookkeeping and notifications performed by `TopicUser.change`, including setting `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` and publishing the level change. In particular, if the reason is still nil, later reads can auto-promote this user's notification level back to tracking, undoing the unsubscribe. Update the preference through the model's change API instead.
